title: feat(plugin-audit, rest): a query of an opted-in saved dataset writes one dataset_query audit row
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DXuamRUC67fx2TTYrFfyuSH)_

domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cz2MxDkQYCC4U8indM

Fixes #31797
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no file under `skills/**` teaches the audit ledger's actions or `AuditPlugin`'s options; `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx` gains a "Dataset queries" section.

## Maintainer quick read

- **What changed:** a deployment can name saved datasets in `new AuditPlugin({ datasetQueryAudit: { datasets: [...] } })`. Each query of one of them through the analytics dataset door then leaves one `dataset_query` row in `sys_audit_log`: who ran it, which dataset, the dimensions and measures selected, the filtered field names and operators (never the values), the row count, and whether it succeeded.
- **Why:** ruling C on this card. An enterprise SIEM must be able to see who read which data under which filter. Reports and dashboards are put together in the browser, so the server only ever sees dataset queries; this records those, and it does not name a report.
- **Risk and rollback:** off by default. With no dataset named, nothing is recorded or buffered, and every door answers as before. Rows are written in batches off the request path. Rollback is reverting this PR.
- **Look first:** (1) `packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-query-audit.ts` `runAuditedDatasetQuery`: only the read is wrapped, so a refusal before it writes nothing; (2) `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/dataset-query-audit.ts` `buildDatasetQueryAuditRow`: what the row holds and that the filter goes through `summarizeExportFilter`; (3) the `queryDataset` hunk in `packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts`.
- **Two-minute check:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/dataset-query-audit.test.ts`. Expect 10 passing cases, among them "a dataset that is not opted in writes no row" and "records no filtered value".
- **What you need to do:** nothing; the seat lands it.

## What changes

**plugin-audit.** A new writer, `dataset-query-audit.ts`, emits `action: 'dataset_query'`. Each row is a run-level row: `record_id` null, the dataset's base object in `object_name`, `user_id` / `actor` / `tenant_id` from the caller's envelope. `metadata` holds `dataset`, `dimensions`, `measures`, `time_dimensions` (names only, when selected), `filter` (field and operator terms from the export writer's `summarizeExportFilter`, every comparand dropped unread), `row_count` and `outcome`. A failed query adds `status` and `error_code`. The delegated-call pair and `impersonated_by` are written as the export row writes them. The writer follows the scope pins `read-audit.ts` set for #8992:

- **Per-dataset opt-in, closed, off by default.** `AuditPlugin`'s new `datasetQueryAudit` option (`datasets`, `maxBatchSize`, `flushIntervalMs`) has the same shape as `readAudit`. No spec change: it is plugin configuration, not authorable metadata, so `Metadata-protocol: none`. A dataset that is not named is dropped before anything is buffered. An empty list builds no batcher.
- **Async batched writes off the request path.** `recordDatasetQuery` on the `audit` slot builds the row when it is called (names and counts only, so the buffer never holds the caller's filter), enqueues it and returns. Rows are written by `createReadAuditBatcher`, the record-view writer's batcher, which now takes an event type parameter and an optional overflow sentence. The query instant is kept through `preserveAudit`, as on record views. A lost batch is reported at `error` once per cause. The named callee `persistDatasetQueryAuditRows` is registered in `check:durability-log-level` and in the swallow census.
- The `sys_audit_log.action` options gain `Dataset Query` / `dataset_query`, with the generated translation leaves for the 11 bundles. The enum ledger (`sys-audit-log-retired-actions.test.ts`) and the label pin list it with its writer. Its shipped surfaces are the unfiltered `recent` and `all_events` views, as for `scim_refused`.

**rest.** `answerDatasetQuery` wraps only the `queryDataset` call in `runAuditedDatasetQuery` (new `analytics-dataset-query-audit.ts`). The event shape is declared structurally, as the export door declares its own. The rules are #31000's, as `data-export-audit.ts` implements them:

- a request the door refuses before the read (identity, the body and selection doors, the dataset's resolution, its parse) hands no event;
- a read that throws hands one event with outcome `failed`, plus the status and machine code `resolveThrownHttpError` reads, never the error's text;
- the batch door calls the same judgment, so each of its queries that reaches the read hands one event.

`AnalyticsRouteHost` gains `resolveAuditService`, and `rest-server.ts` hands it over.

**Overlap with open PRs.** #33491 edits `analytics-routes.ts` (the import of `admitRefusedDatasetHolders`, the refusal-arm hunks near the resolution). This PR's three hunks in that file are elsewhere: one import after `stripReadDecorations`, one member at the end of `AnalyticsRouteHost`, and the `queryDataset` call. `git merge-tree` of this head with each of #33491 and #33512 reports no conflict.

## Tests

The pins were committed first (`4cdb3b2df`) and run red before the fix:

- `plugin-audit` `src/dataset-query-audit.test.ts`: `Error: Cannot find module './dataset-query-audit.js'`. No writer existed.
- `rest` `src/analytics-dataset-query-audit.test.ts`: `Tests 3 failed | 3 passed (6)`. Red: one event per answered query, one failed event after the read started, one event per batch query that reached the read. The three green cases (no event for a refused request, none for an inline definition, a throwing sink does not change the answer) are pins on the absence of an event, so they were green before the door handed any event.

After the fix, with module-level evidence in Verification:

- one row per query of an opted-in dataset (writer over the real ledger, and through `AuditPlugin` and the `audit` slot);
- no row for a dataset that is not opted in, nor with no option at all;
- no event for a query refused before the read (selection without measures 400, unknown dataset 404, unknown body key 400; `queryDataset` never called);
- one `failed` row and event after the read started (503 with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`), the error's text not carried;
- no filtered value anywhere in the row (a sentinel value in `$in`, `$contains`, a nested relation path and an implicit equality);
- the query instant, not the flush instant, on `created_at`; the enqueue returning before the write; a lost batch reported once per cause.

## Acceptance notes

- **Declared narrowing: inline definitions write no row.** The opt-in names saved datasets, and an inline definition's `name` is text the caller chose. Recording inline queries would need a different opt-in key (the base object, say), which this ruling does not decide. The docs section states this edge.
- **A refusal thrown inside `queryDataset` is recorded as a failed read.** The analytics service judges object exposure and dataset fields inside `queryDataset`, and the door cannot tell that throw from a driver fault without reading the service's internals. It follows the export door's precedent, where a refusal from `findData` after the export began is a `failed` row with its status and code: the row says `outcome: failed` with the status and machine code the door answered (a 403 for an exposure refusal). No case pins a 403 row; the 503 case pins the mechanism.
- **The door resolves the `audit` slot for every saved-dataset query.** The opt-in list lives in the writer (one input, the record-view writer's rule), so the door cannot skip the lookup. The cost is a service lookup; the write itself is batched.
- The same dataset name under two packages is one opt-in entry; the row records the name as the door resolved it, not the holding package.
- No ADR-0087 entry is needed: `migrations/entries/semantic/17.audit-log-action-enum-retired.ts` retires `export` / `permission_change` / `restore` only, `packages/spec` has no mirror of the action options, and no other ledger lists them (`git grep -n scim_refused` reaches only plugin-audit and plugin-auth).

## Verification

<details><summary>Package suites and typecheck</summary>

Run on the branch before the last two commits (`3d982b0ac`, then `0f3569f23` for the rest re-run). The last commit `1f741879a` only drops two `as any` casts on the writer's insert and refreshes the tenant audit census; after it, `src/dataset-query-audit.test.ts` + `src/read-audit.test.ts` were run again (`Tests 43 passed (43)`) and plugin-audit `tsc --noEmit` exited 0.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test`: `Test Files 94 passed (94)`, `Tests 1505 passed (1505)`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck`: exit 0 (lock VERDICT command-exit 0).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`: `Test Files 412 passed (412)`, `Tests 8399 passed | 332 skipped (8731)`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck`: exit 0 (lock VERDICT command-exit 0). After moving the import, `analytics-dataset-query-audit.test.ts` + `analytics-routes.test.ts` ran again (`Tests 83 passed (83)`) and rest `tsc --noEmit` exited 0.
- eslint `--no-inline-config` on every changed `.ts` / `.mjs` file: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs`: exit 0 after the new rest pin gained its module-top `@objectstack/objectql` import, which the gate asked for.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run src/sys-metadata-repository.draft-drain.test.ts`, which reads the edited durability gate script: `Tests 11 passed (11)`.

</details>

<details><summary>Derived gate families</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 127 families for this diff, and all 127 were run (`--ran`: 127 derived, 127 run, 0 unrun). Each exit code was captured before any pipe. 121 exited 0 on the first pass. The other six:

- `check-tenant-audit-census` and its `--self-test`: exit 1. This diff adds one write call site (`dataset-query-audit.ts`, insert into `sys_audit_log`, elevated), so the census moved from 314 to 315. Fixed by `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write` plus the six hand-written figures on `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`; both re-run exit 0 (`315 write call sites certified`, self-test `27 cases pass`).
- `pnpm check:i18n`: exit 3, a prerequisite (CLI not built). I built the closure the gate names and re-ran it: exit 0, `all bundles in sync`.
- NOT MEASURED: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (exit 3, shallow clone cannot reach its pinned positive control), `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, needs a whole-repo build), and `spec check:skill-examples` (exit 3, needs the client SDK `dist/`). None of them reads a file this diff changes in a way it depends on; CI runs all three on a full checkout.

The families ran against the tree before `1f741879a`. That commit changes the writer's insert options and the census page, and only the census gate was re-run on it.

</details>
